title: Outlook: expand or collapse all accounts in the folder pane at once
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned folder-pane option and its roadmap scope. The corrected secondary-account licensing statement matches Microsoft's licensing page, although another cited Microsoft page gives conflicting guidance that should be acknowledged.

claims.claim: The feature is a user-chosen action, classified as user-opt-in.
claims.quote: You'll be able to expand or collapse all accounts at once in Outlook's folder pane.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific expand-or-collapse-all-accounts feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "expand or collapse" "accounts"; Outlook expand collapse all accounts folder pane Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy default license 579189. Read policy-management and manage-all-accounts-view; results concerned other folder/group behaviours, not this feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented where this command will appear.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "expand or collapse" "accounts"; Outlook folder pane expand collapse all accounts Cloud Policy Exchange PowerShell Microsoft Graph setting. Read policy-management and manage-all-accounts-view; neither gives this command's location. The roadmap gives none.

claims.claim: Whether Outlook remembers this option's expanded or collapsed state is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "expand or collapse" "accounts". Read roadmap, policy-management and manage-all-accounts-view; no persistence statement for this feature. Search results about classic Outlook folder persistence and message groups do not document this planned option.

claims.claim: No source states that this feature changes the folder pane layout for users who do not use it.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook expand collapse all accounts folder pane Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy default license 579189; Outlook "expand or collapse" "accounts". Read roadmap, policy-management and manage-all-accounts-view; no automatic layout change for this feature is stated.

claims.claim: The separate All Accounts view brings email from connected accounts into one view.
claims.quote: All Accounts brings email from connected accounts into one view; the individual mailboxes remain separate.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents a Cloud Policy controlling whether All Accounts view is shown by default.
claims.quote: Use Cloud Policy to choose whether All Accounts is shown by default in new Outlook for Windows and whether users can change that behavior.

claims.claim: The All Accounts Cloud Policy controls whether users can change that view's configured behaviour.
claims.quote: When user override is disabled, the policy controls the view and users can't change the configured behavior.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Microsoft's licensing page says Outlook for Windows with a Microsoft 365 organisational email address needs a plan including desktop Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Business Basic provides web and mobile Outlook.
claims.quote: The Business Basic plan provides access to productivity tools through the web and mobile versions of Outlook and Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: After an account with a qualifying desktop-app licence is added, secondary Business Basic accounts can be added.
claims.quote: Once you add an account with a qualifying license to Outlook, you can add secondary accounts with licenses for products that don't include the desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.
claims.fix: After the secondary-account licensing sentence, add: "The separate Supported accounts page gives conflicting guidance, stating that accounts associated with SKUs without Outlook client-app licences are not supported." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/get-started/supported-account-types alongside https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/get-started/licensing-options.

claims.claim: After an account with a qualifying desktop-app licence is added, secondary E1 accounts can be added.
claims.quote: Once you add an account with a qualifying license to Outlook, you can add secondary accounts with licenses for products that don't include the desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The option is part of Outlook under the product's existing licensing model, classified as included.
claims.quote: For example, a Business Standard or Business Premium plan provides access to a Microsoft 365 email address and the desktop versions of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no meter, charge or licence specific to this folder-pane option.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook expand collapse all accounts folder pane license pricing meter. Read licensing-options and roadmap; neither names a feature-specific entitlement, price or meter. Search results did not document one.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and .api; summary; Why it matters; Scope: Admin roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin switch or default-setting control is documented for expanding or collapsing all accounts at once.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook folder pane expand collapse all accounts Cloud Policy Exchange PowerShell Microsoft Graph setting. Read policy-management, manage-all-accounts-view; searched Set-OwaMailboxPolicy and Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration. Pane/root-tree settings do not document this all-accounts operation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a display change to accounts in the folder pane rather than new access to mailbox data.
claims.quote: You'll be able to expand or collapse all accounts at once in Outlook's folder pane. You won't need to expand or collapse each account individually.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: As described by the roadmap, the operation expands or collapses accounts rather than adding accounts or changing sign-in.
claims.quote: You'll be able to expand or collapse all accounts at once in Outlook's folder pane.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an action the user takes, not an autonomous operation.
claims.quote: You'll be able to expand or collapse all accounts at once in Outlook's folder pane. You won't need to expand or collapse each account individually.

claims.claim: The cost rating is none for an Outlook layout option within the already licensed product.
claims.quote: For example, a Business Standard or Business Premium plan provides access to a Microsoft 365 email address and the desktop versions of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not mention classic Outlook.
